attempts.summary: Built a 3-segment topology (lan-a: node3↔node1, transit: node1↔node2, lan-b: node2↔node4) on top of the extra NICs each node already had, discovered adjacency via ARP/ping probing (default mgmt NICs are all flat on 10.100.120.0/24 and unrelated to the data path). Configured VyOS (node1) with a source-NAT masquerade rule on its transit interface (eth1) for lan-a traffic, and OPNsense (node2) with a hybrid-mode outbound NAT masquerade rule on its lan-b interface (vtnet2) for transit-sourced traffic, plus matching pass rules on both opt interfaces. node4 runs a persistent (systemd) Python HTTP server on 8080. Verified with tcpdump on node1's transit link (source rewritten to node1's transit IP 10.50.20.1) and node2's lan-b link (source rewritten again to node2's lan-b IP 10.50.30.254), and node4's HTTP access log records the connection as arriving purely from 10.50.30.254 — never node3's or node1's real address. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes (node3, node1, node4, node2), confirming boot-identity change (boot_id / kern.boottime) on each and re-verifying full end-to-end connectivity and correct double-NAT source (10.50.30.254) after every restart.
